<!-- dsh-action:v1 kind=finding fingerprint=8174a6388d87ef2156bf84814673ba85e6497846faf0971ccafc717733c57e1b -->

### 🟡 Medium · Advance NER evaluation_version so cached reviews are rescored

The new padding removal and per-entity trim change the BIO tags produced for the same prediction text (e.g. `<person> Alice </person> won` changes from `['O','O']` to `['B-PER','O']`), yet every NER adapter keeps `evaluation_version='v1.1'` (cross_ner `v1.2`). `build_benchmark_identity` folds `evaluation_version` into the benchmark cache fingerprint, and `cache_source_for_identity` returns the previous cache source whenever the fingerprint matches, so a supported `use_cache` resume after upgrading silently reuses review rows whose `y_pred` was computed by the old, dropped-entity path; the fix is never applied to those samples. This module already treats span-alignment changes as requiring rescoring: `test_ner_reviews_require_rescoring_after_span_alignment_changes` and the comment on the cross_ner `v1.2` bump ("when it started scoring each subset with its own labels").

**Evidence:** evalscope/evaluation_versioning.py:206-215 includes `evaluation_version` in the identity payload/fingerprint, and :164-171 treats a matching fingerprint as reusable; the review cache then serves the stored SampleScore keyed only by sample_id (evalscope/api/evaluator/cache.py:185-223). All 22 NER adapters (e.g. evalscope/benchmarks/ner/conll2003_adapter.py:9) remain v1.1, and tests/benchmark/test_ner_span_alignment.py:133 still asserts 'v1.1'/'v1.2'.

**Suggested change:**

Bump `evaluation_version` for the NER adapters (v1.1 -> v1.2; cross_ner v1.2 -> v1.3), update the version expectation in `test_ner_benchmark_scores_preserve_entity_boundaries`, and note that existing work dirs need `rerun_review=True` to pick up the new alignment.

<sub>regression · confidence 82%</sub>
